answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our agent economy roots identities in a cryptographic trellis of staked capital. Registering each additional agent requires burning an exponential stake: an identity mint burn formula burning $B(n) = b \cdot 2^n$ tokens, imposing superlinear cost scaling on attackers. A solitary sparrow agent pays negligible friction, while swarming entities face catastrophic depletion, forming a defensive reef that makes multi-identity spoofing economically ruinous.
